title: Pricing/Packaging scratchpad — token math & tier ideas
body:
Goal: quick back-of-envelope for token economics + simple tier ideas. Mostly notes to self; messy.

Assumptions (very rough):
- Average generated tokens per API call (chat): 75 tokens output + 20 tokens input = 95 tokens total (round to 100 for easy math).
- Embedding call: average doc chunk = 512 tokens.
- Baseline infra cost per 1k tokens served (amortized compute + network + storage + orchestration): $0.002 per 1k tokens (assume optimized quantized LLMs on shared infra).
  - Notes: this is an assumption for hosted/shared capacity; dedicated/private will be higher per-customer but sold as committed capacity.
- Additional overhead (monitoring, infra ops, customer support, billing) add ~30% margin on top of infra cost.
- Target gross margin for hosted API: 60% (i.e., price needs to be ~2.5x the infra+overhead).

Quick math examples:
1) Per-token cost basis:
- Infra: $0.002 / 1k = $0.000002 per token
- +30% overhead -> $0.0000026 per token
- Price target for 60% gross margin -> price_per_token = cost / (1 - 0.6) = 0.0000026 / 0.4 = $0.0000065 per token -> ~ $0.0000065
  - Per 1k tokens: $0.0065 (rounded $0.006)

2) Chat API example (100 tokens per call):
- Cost per call (infra+ovhd): 100 * $0.0000026 = $0.00026
- Price (60% margin) -> $0.00065 per call -> ~ $0.65 per 1k calls (or $0.0065 per 1k tokens consistent with above)

3) Embeddings example (512 tokens per call):
- Infra cost: 512 * $0.000002 = $0.001024
- +30% -> $0.00133
- Price for 60% margin -> $0.00333 per embedding call (~$3.33 per 1k embedding calls at 512 tokens each)

Check against market signals (sanity):
- If we price at $0.006 per 1k tokens, that is roughly in-line with low-cost self-hosted inference offering; higher-quality/distil models will be priced higher. 
- Embedding pricing needs to be separate unit (per vector) rather than raw token-only, since memory/IO dominates and customer patterns differ.

Tiering primitives to play with:
- Included monthly tokens (pooled across endpoints)
- Token carryover ? (probably no, keep simple)
- Rate limits (TPS) tied to tier and can be burstable with paid add-ons
- SLA (uptime & latency SLO) as add-on / higher tiers
- Dedicated capacity as separate product (monthly commit), not a tier within hosted
- Embedding units counted differently: e.g., per-embedding-unit where 1 unit ~= 512 tokens or 1 call (explicit metric)

Draft tier ideas (hosted API):
- Free / Starter (PLG funnel): 100k tokens/month, 30 req/min, basic analytics, email support (encourage trial)
- Developer: $20/month -> 10M tokens/month (~$0.002 per 1k tokens effective cost to user) + higher rate limit (200 rpm), basic usage analytics, API keys management
  - Note: at our price baseline $0.0065 / 1k tokens, 10M tokens revenue = $65/mo; $20 is subsidized to accelerate adoption. Need credits/grace period logic.
- Startup: $250/month -> 200M tokens/month + SSO, team seats, webhooks, better analytics, higher rate limits
  - Revenue estimate: at baseline pricing 200M tokens => $1,300/month. We can either: a) price below baseline to be competitive, b) price near baseline and offer committed discount for startups.
- Scale: $2,500/month -> 2B tokens/month + 24/7 support, SLA, burst priority
- Enterprise: custom pricing -> dedicated options, private deployment, contractual SLAs, extensive observability + onboarding services

Notes on committing discounts / credits:
- Offer committed volume discounts (e.g., 10-30%) depending on term and whether they take Redwood Dedicated/Private.
- For mid-size customers, selling guaranteed monthly committed tokens simplifies budgeting and unlocks margin predictability.

Embed vs gen pricing separation:
- Embedding pricing should be per-embedding (per vector) or per-chunk processed, with a thinner marginal cost but higher memory/IO footprint. Example: $0.0007 per embedding (512 token chunk) at baseline calculations -> needs sanity check vs competitors.

Other levers to control economics:
- Batching & caching recommendations (Optimize product) can be monetized as features or provided for free to reduce unit cost
- Quantization/ model selection routing: route cheaper requests to quantized variants automatically unless quality guardrails trigger
- Autoscaling/burst: incentivize smoothing usage via credits or lower price for consistent usage

Open questions / TODOs:
- Recompute infra cost with real infra numbers: GPU hours, throughput (tokens/sec), average seq length distribution across customers. (Ask infra for 1Q real numbers.)
- Should we align pricing units to tokens or to requests? Tokens more accurate for cost recovery but less intuitive for some customers (esp. embeddings). Consider dual-metric: tokens for generation, vectors for embeddings.
- Decide whether free tier should limit models (only smaller models) to protect capacity and funnel to paid tiers.
- How to handle multi-model pricing (e.g., large model = price multiplier)? Simpler UX: model categories (small/medium/large) with per-token multiplier.
- Rate limit mapping to tiers: need concrete TPS numbers. Get SRE guidance on safe default per-tier TPS for hosted cluster.

Quick action items:
- Pull 3-month token distribution (by seq length) from infra telemetry (ask infra team: Noah).
- Benchmark per-1k-token cost for our optimized runtime on shared hosted infra (include egress/network) — ask serving-runtime (Riley) for updated numbers.
- Draft simple pricing page copy for PLG funnel + pricing calculator (estimate revenue given tokens) — next week.

Random notes (brain dump):
- For developer tier, use aggressive subsidized price to lower barrier (consider credits rather than monthly discount).
- Consider embedding mini-tier: low-cost bulk embedding for vector DB ingestion (one-off ingestion credits) vs per-request inference embedding.
- For Dedicated customers, sell per-GPU node pricing with token-equivalent mapping for forecasting.

End of scratchpad.

Questions I want to answer before next draft:
- What is true marginal cost per 1k tokens on hosted infra? (urgent)
- Are we comfortable exposing per-token as the primary metric in marketing? (pros/cons)
- How will we present embeddings (per vector vs per token) to avoid confusion?

References/links: confluence:PRICING-DRAFT-2026 (model categories), JIRA:PRIC-112 (pricing experiments), github:repo/issue/987 (pricing calculator prototype)
